newsitem.title: USA: A few protesters greet Thatcher during Kansas visit.
newsitem.headline: A few protesters greet Thatcher during Kansas visit.

text.p: Former British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher was heckled by a small group of Irish nationalist sympathisers in Kansas on Wednesday as she helped dedicate a chapel with considerable personal significance for her.
The chapel, where Thatcher's father was once a lay minister, was moved stone by stone from the family's hometown in Grantham, England, to Baker University in Baldwin City, Kansas.
Between 12 and 20 protesters shouted slogans during the dedication ceremony, which attracted about 3,500 people, said John Fuller, director of news services for the school.
"I think they shouted 'Go Home'," he said. "They were trying to shout in unison, but they weren't doing a very good job."
Daniel Lambert, the university's president, said he expected the protesters were sympathisers of the Irish Republican Army, but said their chanting was barely audible.

Baker University obtained the small stone chapel, which seats about 100 people, after it was closed down seven or eight years ago, Lambert said. It was moved from Britain, birthplace of the Methodist religion, because the school wanted a chapel tied to its Methodist heritage.
